newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia begins deporting Timor conference activists.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia begins deporting Timor conference activists.

text.p: Malaysia began deporting on Sunday foreign activists who participated in a controversial conference on East Timor which was broken up by youths allied to the government, immigration officials said.

An immigration department spokesman at the Kuala Lumpur international airport said 16 activists were put on four different flights on Sunday morning. They included five Australians, four Americans, three Japanese, two Portuguese and two Sri Lankans.
He said another group is scheduled to leave on Sunday while others are still awaiting tickets.

The 46 foreign activists, including two Roman Catholic bishops -- Rev. Aloisuis Nobulo Somo of Japan and the Rev. Hilton Deakin of Melbourne, Australia -- were detained by police after the meeting was disrupted by a youth group who stormed into it shouting slogans and singing patriotic songs.
Seven members of the youth group along with 59 Malaysian human rights group activists and two foreign jounalists were also detained.
A Malaysian minister said earlier this week that the government did not want the conference to take place because it could harm bilateral ties with Indonesia.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and now rules the territory in defiance of the United Nations.
The youth group, calling itself the Malaysian Action Front, drew riot police to a hotel in central Kuala Lumpur after they stormed into the meeting.

Malaysian Action Front Secretary-General Saifudin Nasution said the group comprised youth groups allied to the three main political parties in Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's coalition -- the United Malays National Organisation, the Malaysian Chinese Association and the Malaysian Indian Congress.
Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said earlier this week the government strongly objected to the meeting and would seek legal ways of stopping it.
The meeting was being held ahead of Tuesday's anniversary of the 1991 killing by Indonesian troops of at least 50 demonstrators in East Timor's capital of Dili.

Indonesia invaded East Timor in December 1975 and annexed it the following year. The United Nations still recognises Lisbon as the administering authority in the territory, located in the far east of the Indonesian archipelago.
